chunks: And al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Abu Talib 'Abd Allah ibn al-Salt, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, concerning:

A mouse falls into the well, and a man performs wudu (ablution) from it and prays while he does not know. Should he repeat the salat (prayer) and wash his garment? He said: He does not repeat the salat (prayer), and he does not wash his garment.

key_terms.الْبِئْرِ: the well from which the water was taken
key_terms.الْفَأْرَةِ: a mouse; the animal mentioned as falling into the well
key_terms.فَيَتَوَضَّأُ: he performs wudu (ablution) using that water
key_terms.لَا يَعْلَمُ: he does not know; indicating ignorance of the situation at the time

ai.seo_question: If a mouse fell into a well and someone unknowingly used its water for wudu (ablution) and salat (prayer), must he repeat the prayer and wash his clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a person who used water from a well after a mouse had fallen into it without his knowledge. Imam Abu 'Abd Allah عليه السلام states that he does not need to repeat the salat (prayer) nor wash his garment, indicating no retroactive obligation in this case.
